newsitem.title: USA: Six groups sue U.S. EPA over new clean air rules.
newsitem.headline: Six groups sue U.S. EPA over new clean air rules.

text.p: The American Trucking Associations, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and four other groups filed a lawsuit Friday challenging the new U.S. clean air standards.
The Environmental Protection Agency this week issued controversial rules setting strict new limits on smog-forming ozone beginning in 2004 and fine particles beginning in 2005.

The six groups said they were suing to overturn the smog and soot standards on the grounds that EPA had failed to comply with a 1996 law that requires agencies to consider the impact new rules will have on small businesses, and that the standards were based on "inadequate science."

"The new standards -- which offer no verifiable health benefits -- will hamstring economic growth and eliminate badly needed jobs in cities and towns nationwide," said Thomas Donohue, president of the American Trucking Associations, which represents the trucking industry.
The trucking group and U.S. Chamber were joined by the National Coalition of Petroleum Retailers, and three freight companies.

EPA Administrator Carol Browner has repeatedly defended the new rules saying that independently-reviewed science showed that existing smog and soot standards were not good enough to protect public health.
And she said the new standards were unlikely to hammer small businesses, because power plants and industrial plants would be the main targets for pollution controls to meet the stricter limits.
